To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the attitudes that significantly influence behavioral intention (BI), the intention to use information and communications technologies (ICTs), need to be at a specific specificity, with the BI on two aspects: same evaluation target, and same evaluation time.

(a). Attitudes toward using a specific system at a particular time can significantly influence the intention to use the same system at the same time; (b). The relationships between attitudes and intentions remain the same if measured at the same point in time regardless of use stages.

(1) attitude's influence on BI is contingent on the evaluation target and time specificity of attitude and BI; (2) the relationships among attitude and BI are stable over time; (3) different types of attitudes have different temporal effects; (4) the omission of important mediating factors may lead to misleading results; and (5) attitude can explain a large proportion of the variance in BI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the complexity of attitude.
the following questions: (1) How do attitudes influence behavioral intention? (2) How do the different attitudes and behavioral intention change over time?
the complexity of different types and dynamics of attitudes in initial ICT use and continued use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
attitude is a complex construct that has both conceptual and operational complexities.

the attitudes toward the use of ICTs have different influences on the intention to use ICTs at different stages of use, and the influence of attitude on BI can be explained by the different mediating factors.

the attitude that significantly influences intention to continue using an IS needs to be at the same evaluation target as the intention and the same evaluation period as the intention; the attitude that significantly predicts the intention to use an IS needs to have the same evaluation target with the intention and the evaluation period that precedes the intention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attitude is a very important factor in understanding ICT use.
attitudes are a key determinant for behavioral intention, but the effect is not always significant.
attitudes are important for understanding and explaining ICT use behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attitude is an important factor in explaining the intention to use information systems.
the effects of attitudes on intention can be explained by the specificity of the attitudes and intention, and the time of measurement.
attitude is a critical construct in information systems (IS).
